name: Acme Universal Safezone 9
lm_rationale: Expert Global Consultants: chittorgarh 2026 SME tracker shows 1 issue (₹66.24 Cr), 0% positive, -7.99% avg listing gain. IPOPlatform shows 21 SME IPOs all-time with 17 (81%) positive listings, but 14 of 21 (67%) now trade below issue price.
net_proceeds: ₹3.62 Cr for a solar power plant, ₹8.96 Cr for additional machinery and ₹8.00 Cr for working capital (₹20.58 Cr identified). The rest goes to unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes, capped together at 35% of gross proceeds.
key_risks: Top 10 customers made up 47.71% of FY26 sales. Borrowings rose from ₹44.51 Cr to ₹58.05 Cr over FY24-FY26 with interest cover of 1.80x. Two EPCG authorisations carry export obligations running to November 2030.
market_moat: BIS IS 15298-certified safety footwear across 15 product lines, made in four plants in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh with 43,15,000 pairs a year of installed capacity. The company also exports to the Gulf, Africa and Europe.
management: Promoters Nitin Tiwari and Ruchi Tiwari; 94.88% pre-issue promoter holding drops to 69.73% post-issue.
prose_business: Acme Universal Safezone 9 makes industrial safety shoes (EVA-rubber, nitrile rubber and PVC soles) for construction, oil and gas, mining, engineering, automotive and chemical plants. It sells through direct institutional sales, distributors, dealers and e-commerce, and exports to markets including the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Nigeria and the Netherlands.
highlight_dev: On 25 Sep 2026 the company allotted 14,38,400 anchor shares at ₹71 (₹10.21 Cr) to Viney Growth Fund, Innovative Vision Fund and Tiger Strategies Fund – I.
sector_outlook: The RHP, citing DGFT data, shows India's safety-footwear exports rising from INR 647.75 crore in FY2021 to INR 959.19 crore in FY2025.
gov_scheme: The company imported capital machinery at concessional duty under the EPCG Scheme and holds two authorisations with export obligations running to November 2030.
peer_sentence: At 23.14x post-issue P/E, the issue is below Liberty Shoes Ltd (40.82x) and Superhouse Ltd (54.74x) and slightly above Mallcom (India) Ltd (20.76x) in the RHP peer table (average 38.77x).
verdict_reason: P/BV of 1.89x, but ROCE of 5.54%, D/E of 1.10 and a volatile PAT history
why: Revenue grew steadily to ₹205.90 Cr in FY26 (+9.90%), but PAT has swung from ₹7.56 Cr to ₹0.80 Cr and back to ₹5.86 Cr, with a thin 2.77% PAT margin and 5.54% ROCE. At ₹71 the stock trades at 1.89x book and a 23.14x post-issue P/E, below the RHP peer average of 38.77x but above Mallcom's 20.76x. Proceeds mostly go to machinery, solar and working capital, and up to 35% can go to unidentified acquisitions and GCP. Expert Global's one 2026 listing opened -7.99%, although its longer SME record has 81% positive listings. The main risk is rising debt (D/E 1.10, interest cover 1.80x) against low returns on capital.
suggestion: Watch; low book multiple, but thin margins and weak returns make it a long-term hold at best, and listing gains are uncertain
discrepancies: chittorgarh post-issue P/E 23.13x vs 23.14x computed from RHP PAT ₹585.73 lakh / 1,90,93,420 shares (EPS 3.0677); rounding only
chittorgarh PAT margin 2.84% is on revenue from operations (RHP KPI); on total income ₹21,116.15 lakh it is 2.77%. Card uses 2.77% per brief
chittorgarh shows no ROE; RHP discloses only RoNW 11.75% (PAT / average net worth), used for both fields
RHP internal inconsistency: FY25 Basic EPS shown as 0.59 (adjusted, Basis for Issue Price), 67.42 (KPI table) and 17.19 (peer KPI comparison); FY26 EPS 4.17 is consistent and used
RHP peer KPI table shows Superhouse FY25/FY24 net worth as '1.40%'/'2.08%' (typo); not used
RHP risk factor 18 still refers to 'this DRHP' and states the capex does not add installed capacity
